ImageDescription.value:
Name: Ramla-British Military Cemetery
Description: 5731 martyrs who were killed or died during their service or service in Israel from the days of World War I until the end of the British Mandate in Palestine in 1948 were buried there. ImageDescription.value:
Name: Ramla-British Military Cemetery
Description: The cemetery was established after World War I for the burial of military and police personnel who died in wars and violent events (British and others) of all religions, until the end of the Mandate in Israel. The site is the largest of the British military cemeteries and approximately 4,500 fallen were buried there.

pages.title: File:128631 ramla-kabru - tombstone of a british pilot-january PikiWiki Israel.jpg

ObjectName.value: 128631 ramla-kabru - tombstone of a british pilot-january PikiWiki Israel

Categories.value: Ramleh War Cemetery|The British-Israeli Air Incident|Images from the Pikiwiki project|Template Unknown (author)|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation

ImageDescription.value:
Name: Ramla-Kabru - Tombstone of a British Pilot-January
Description: In Operation Horev during the War of Independence, 5 British fighter planes were shot down in the western Negev by the young Israeli Air Force. 2 British pilots died in the crash, one of whom is buried in Ramla. The planes were apparently mistakenly identified as Egyptian enemy planes. At the time, the incident was kept quiet to avoid a diplomatic confrontation
